capital.heading: 12 instruments. A repriced diamond deal, budget support from the AfDB and the OPEC Fund, a bank loan for water and power, and World Bank programmes for schools, water, power and health.

register.name: Infrastructure loan from Standard Chartered Bank Botswana
register.detail: Authorised by Parliament, March 2026 · Euribor + 1.6% · 15 years, five years’ grace
register.note: Backed by a MIGA guarantee, as reported by the Government
register.text: A commercial loan for four projects: rehabilitating the water networks of Kanye, Moshupa and Molepolole, upgrading the Mambo wastewater scheme in Francistown, and the second phase of the North-West Transmission Grid Connection. The Government reports a guarantee from the World Bank Group’s Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency. It carries water and energy, two of the seven standards.

register.name: Debswana sales agreement with De Beers
register.detail: Signed February 2025 · Ten-year sales agreement · Licences extended to July 2054
register.note: Share of Debswana’s output sold by the Okavango Diamond Company: 30% for five years, then 40%
register.text: The Okavango Diamond Company sells 30% of Debswana’s rough diamonds for the first five years and 40% for the next five, with a possible five-year extension at an equal split. Debswana’s mining licences are extended by 25 years, from August 2029 to July 2054, and De Beers commits BWP 1 billion upfront to a Diamonds for Development Fund.

register.name: Governance and Economic Resilience Support Program, additional financing
register.detail: Approved 25 March 2026 · Signed 20 September 2026 · Policy-based loan
register.note: OPEC Fund, co-financed with the African Development Bank; total cost $674M
register.text: A policy-based loan from the OPEC Fund to the Republic of Botswana, co-financed with the African Development Bank in a programme with a total cost of $674 million. It follows the OPEC Fund’s first loan under the programme, of $200 million in 2025. Budget support of this kind protects the public spending on which the seven standards depend.

register.name: Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL)
register.note: World Bank financing for participation and learning in schools
register.text: A World Bank operation approved on 30 July 2026, named for its two aims: more children taking part in school and better learning. Education is one of the seven standards, and fewer than half of Botswana’s children read a simple text by the end of primary school (World Bank, 2011).

register.name: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Project
register.detail: Approved 9 October 2025 · Announced 26 January 2026 · Five years
register.text: Builds an electronic system that tracks medical supplies from central warehouses to remote health posts, a climate-resilient National Drug Quality Control Laboratory and upgrades to the National Public Health Laboratory, with trained rapid response teams. The Ministry of Health implements it with the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority. It strengthens health, the sixth of the seven standards.

register.name: Governance and Economic Resilience Support Program
register.detail: Approved 18 June 2025 · Signed 12 August 2025 · Policy-based loan
register.note: OPEC Fund, co-financed with the African Development Bank; total cost $504M
register.text: A policy-based loan from the OPEC Fund that co-financed, with the African Development Bank, a programme with a total cost of $504 million for the 2025/26 budget. It supported reforms in fiscal transparency, revenue collection and private-sector growth as diamond revenue fell. Budget support of this kind protects the public spending on which the seven standards depend.

register.name: Renewable Energy Support and Access Accelerator Project
register.detail: Approved 11 July 2024 · First World Bank lending for renewable energy in Botswana
register.note: World Bank loan; a $30m loan and $4m grant from the Green Climate Fund alongside
register.text: The World Bank’s first lending operation for renewable energy in Botswana. It invests in the grid so that the first wave of 335 MW of private renewable projects can be integrated, builds the country’s first 50 MW utility-scale battery storage system, and extends the grid to rural villages. It carries energy, one of the seven standards.

register.name: Botswana Renewable Energy Scale Up Support
register.detail: ESMAP technical assistance grant · Announced with RESA, July 2024
register.note: Solar, wind and storage technical assistance
register.text: A $3.5 million technical assistance grant from ESMAP, the World Bank’s energy programme, announced alongside the renewable energy project of July 2024, for solar, wind and storage.

register.name: Economic Resilience and Green Recovery Development Policy Loan II
register.detail: Announced 16 June 2023 · Second of two operations
register.text: Supports reforms that make social spending more responsive to shocks, including climate shocks; strengthen financial regulation so that small businesses can formalise and borrow; and advance universal energy access and the shift to renewable energy. It bears on livelihood and energy among the seven standards.

register.name: Programmatic Economic Resilience and Green Recovery Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Announced 11 June 2021 · First World Bank budget support for Botswana
register.note: World Bank budget support, first of two operations
register.text: Supported the Economic Recovery and Transformation Plan after COVID-19: a Single Social Registry to target social spending on the most vulnerable, access to finance for small businesses, and renewable power from independent producers and rooftop solar. It was the first World Bank budget support operation for Botswana.

register.name: Emergency Water Security and Efficiency Project
register.detail: Approved 1 March 2017 · Response to the 2015–2016 drought
register.note: World Bank loan to the Republic of Botswana
register.text: Responds to the 2015–2016 drought by improving water supply in drought-vulnerable areas, wastewater management and the efficiency of the Water Utilities Corporation. About 460,000 people stand to gain from upgraded water supply and about 177,000 from better wastewater treatment.

register.name: Governance and Economic Resilience Support Programme
register.detail: Approved May 2025 · One-year budget support for 2025/26
register.note: African Development Bank general budget support
register.text: A one-year general budget support operation for the 2025/26 fiscal year, to cushion Botswana against the fall in diamond revenue while it advances reforms in fiscal transparency, revenue collection and private-sector growth. It also targets micro, small and medium enterprises, particularly those led by women and young people. It bears on livelihood, the weakest of the seven standards in Botswana.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Diamonds
items.label: Of exports, IMF, 2025
items.text: About a quarter of GDP. The 2025 agreement raises the state’s share of Debswana’s sales to 30%, then 40%.
items.alt: A diamond mine in the Kalahari, Botswana

items.name: The Sun
items.label: Renewable share of electricity output, 2021
items.text: A grid run almost wholly on coal, under a desert sun. The largest gap between asset and use on this page.
items.alt: The Kalahari under a desert sun

items.name: The Delta
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: The Okavango and its woodlands: a wildlife economy run on high-value, low-volume terms.
items.alt: The Okavango Delta from the air

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Rangeland and cattle across nearly half the country, while 18.2% of people are undernourished.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Two in three live in towns and cities.

items.name: Mmadinare Solar Complex, Scatec
items.text: Botswana’s first utility-scale renewable independent power producer, near Selebi-Phikwe, selling solar power to Botswana Power Corporation.

items.name: Lenmed Hospital Group
items.text: Runs 19 hospitals in Botswana, South Africa, Ghana and Mozambique; an IFC loan supports new facilities, medical equipment and staff.

items.name: Peo Finance
items.text: A non-bank micro lender making personal loans, mainly to government employees, for education, farming and home improvement. IFC agreed to lend it up to $40 million equivalent.
